name: Chakuli Pitha
subtitle: soft fermented rice and urad pancakes, thicker and paler than a dosa

ingredients.note: helps the batter ferment and browns the edges

prepNotes: Soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds in another, both in plenty of water, for 6 hours.
Grind the dal first with 150ml water until it is white, fluffy and holds a peak; then grind the rice with 200ml water to a fine batter with the faintest grit.
Combine the two, beat in the sugar with your hand for a minute, cover loosely and ferment 8 to 10 hours in a warm spot until risen and bubbly.
Salt the batter only after fermenting. Salt slows the rise.

steps.text: Stir the salt into the fermented batter and let it down with water until it is the consistency of thick cream, thicker than dosa batter.
steps.tip: Stir gently. Beating hard knocks out the air you spent all night building.

steps.text: Heat a flat tawa over medium until a drop of water skitters and vanishes in about 2 seconds.
Rub the surface with half an onion or a scrunched paper towel dipped in oil and wipe off the excess.
Pour a ladleful into the centre and spread it with the back of the ladle in one slow spiral to about 15cm. Chakuli is meant to be thick and soft, not lace-thin.
steps.tip: One pass only. Going back over a setting batter tears holes in it.

steps.text: Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the rim and cook 2 minutes, until the top loses its shine and small holes open across the surface.
Flip and cook the second side 1 minute, until it is set and speckled pale gold.
steps.tip: Chakuli should stay soft and blond. If it is crisp and brown you have the tawa too hot.

steps.text: Slide it off and repeat, wiping and re-oiling the tawa between each one and dropping the heat a notch if they start browning too fast.
Stack them under a cloth as you go so they steam each other soft, and serve hot with ghuguni or a mustardy vegetable curry.

storage: The batter keeps 3 days refrigerated and gets tangier each day; bring it to room temperature before using. Cooked chakuli keep 1 day wrapped in a cloth and reheat in 30 seconds on a warm tawa.
